public_rationale: OpenAI documented elevated errors affecting free users on November 7, 2025, establishing the service-degradation condition [e1]. Its June 2026 adoption report describes growth since July 2023 using data combining Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans [e2]. Neither source establishes whether affected free users left because of the degradation and thereby reduced user growth [e1, e2]. Aggregate adoption growth does not rule out growth being lower than it would otherwise have been, leaving the causal forecast unresolved [e2].
limitations: The incident record does not measure subsequent retention or departures.
The adoption report does not isolate affected free users or estimate growth without the degradation.

statement.excerpt: If free users face service degradation, they will bounce off the product, as their use is likely far more fleeting than a paid user, which will begin to erode OpenAI's growth.
statement.document_title: OpenAI Is A Systemic Risk To The Tech Industry

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that degradation causes affected free users to leave or stop returning, reducing user growth relative to what would otherwise have occurred.
Growth can remain positive while being reduced by departures. Aggregate growth alone therefore cannot disprove the claim.
No deadline, minimum departure rate, or length of degradation is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Free-user degradation occurs, followed by measured departures and credible evidence that those departures reduced OpenAI's user growth.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible analysis of affected free-user cohorts shows that degradation did not cause departures or reduce growth during the identified episode.
